title: Crease-following rings: the path between anchors hugs the nearest groove, and a one-click ring along the groove nearest a point
description: From CRAW-58 (agent segmenting IMG_4111 from scratch, friction log F7/F9/F13/F14): the agent's best rings came from clicking ~7 points along a groove from three views; the connection tool cut at the wrong place on tapering parts, and cross-field rings (CRAW-31) mostly fall back on the crawfish (field noise, ~1450 singularities, and the field follows global curvature, not the specific groove). Wanted: (a) a ring mode where the path between anchors is a shortest path on a crease-weighted cost (intelligent-scissors / magnetic lasso: edges along a valley are cheap, edges across one expensive), so the ring hugs the groove and the user only adds anchors where it jumps; (b) a one-click 'ring along this groove': from a clicked point find the nearest crease and follow it around the limb back to the start. Crease signal candidates: (1) the Hopf-differential bend field and its diffused CreaseField heat map from PATCH-104 (archived; code in tag archive/patch-104, readable with git show archive/patch-104:<path>; NDirectionField stored vertexBend = Hopf differential magnitude per vertex, CreaseField diffused it over ~one quad edge). PATCH-104 found it worked as a heat map but is unsigned anisotropy: thin tubes read uniformly bright, so it needed a local-maximum-across-the-path / peakedness test; (2) CrestLineDetector valley lines (signed: grooves are concave valleys, ridges should not attract); (3) min principal curvature from the curvature tensor CurvatureConstraints already computes. Pick by measurement, not by taste. The cost field is a per-mesh value: provide it the way the metric is provided (a node with a typed output port the ring takes, wired on save; no hidden per-mesh caches).
definition-of-done: 1. A crease mode for ring segments (alongside geodesic and the CRAW-31 field modes if landed), selectable per ring, saved in the DSL and reloaded element-exact. 2. A one-click groove ring in the ring tool: click near a groove, the ring follows it around the part and closes; refused with a reason when no closed groove is found. 3. Evaluation on the user's IMG_4109 segmentation (fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl, 82 rings): for each user ring, one click at a point on that ring produces a groove ring; report how many land on the user's ring (mean distance under a stated fraction of ring radius) vs the geodesic preview ring, plus mean distance to valley creases. 4. Crawfish timings: building the crease field and tracing one ring (target: field built once in a few seconds, a ring in under ~100 ms). 5. Fertility does not regress; existing ring fingerprints unchanged. 6. Unit test on a procedural surface with an analytic groove (e.g. a tube with a circumferential notch): the crease ring lies in the notch within a tolerance, the geodesic one does not.
testing-plan: Procedural notch-tube unit test; benchmark over the user's 82 crawfish rings; F5 entry on a crawfish copy to click grooves by hand.
changes-made: Crease mode for ring segments: RingSegmentMode {GEODESIC, CREASE} (same shape as CRAW-31's enum, so the two merge as a union of values). spline_ring gains mode= ("geodesic" default, "crease") and creases= (typed SURFACE_CREASES port from the new surface_creases node, required in crease mode, refused with a wiring hint otherwise). RingDslWriter.wireSurfaceMetric became wireRingInputs (as in CRAW-31): it still wires metric=, and for every crease-mode ring adds creases = surface_creases(geometry=surface.geometry) after its surface_metric (one per surface) and creases=creases.creases after metric=; withMode writes/removes mode= in place. RingTool keeps confirmedMode/draftMode/savedModeByStatement through confirm, re-open, undo/redo (RingToolState), save and graph adoption.

SurfaceCreases (data/paths): per-vertex valley strength in [0,1] and per-edge crease cost (length x (0.05 + 0.95 x (1 - mean end strength))). of(mesh) uses the concave principal curvature from PrincipalDirectionField (kappaMax on an outward-wound mesh, -kappaMin on an inward one, decided by the signed volume), Jacobi-diffused over 3 mean edges together with the across-groove line tensor, saturated at the 95th percentile with the median curvature magnitude as floor (a plain tube saturates nowhere). acrossGroove holds the smoothed across-groove line per vertex. Never written after it is built.

AuthoredSplineRing crease mode: the reference the supporting anchors are fitted to is the cheapest closed crease path through the authored anchors in order, once round the part. Once-round is a double cover of a slab (+-1 plane-loop radius) about the ring plane, with a seam half-plane from the plane loop's centre through the first anchor; one Dijkstra per span over both sheets, each span takes its cheaper sheet and, when the parity is even, the span losing least flips. traceGroove(click, girdleNormal, depth) is the one-click groove ring: nearest groove vertex (strength >= 0.5) within 0.15 plane-loop radii, climbed to the groove bottom, ringed in the plane normal to the groove's smoothed across line, falling back to the girdling plane; refused with a reason when no groove is in reach, no crease path closes, or less than half the ring runs in a groove. grooveNormal is the written normal it used, so a save reloads the same ring.

Ring tool keys: V = groove ring at the hovered point (drafts a crease-mode ring; Enter confirms, Ctrl+S saves mode="crease" and wires surface_creases), T = switch the draft between geodesic and crease (one undoable edit). The creases are the graph's surface_creases output when one exists, else measured once per model and logged. RingScene.refreshControls rebuilds the hints (same method CRAW-31 adds).

Signal chosen by measurement (GrooveRingBenchmark, -Dbenchmark.ringGraph=tmp/crawfish_rings.dsl, IMG_4109 469k vertices / 938k faces; one click at each of the 82 saved rings' first anchor; landed = symmetric mean distance to the saved ring < 0.1 of its mean radius, near < 0.2; valley = CrestLineDetector valley lines on the inward-wound copy). geodesic preview (the hover ring the tool drafts): 4 landed, 7 near, 0 refused, mean off 1.81 r, 0.271 r from valleys, 36 ms. concave curvature (chosen): 5 / 6 / 16 refused, 1.59 r, 0.108 r from valleys, 117 ms mean, 407 worst. valley crest lines: 2 / 4 / 11, 2.02 r, 0.128 r. convex curvature (ridges, sanity): 0 / 1 / 44 refused, 0.424 r. Hopf bend (unsigned, needs a 4.4 s cross field): 6 / 10 / 18, 1.65 r, 0.174 r. Concave curvature is chosen: closest to the valleys, fewest refusals of the groove signals, and no cross-field solve; the bend's 1-ring landing edge is inside noise and it hugs ridges and tubes as PATCH-104 found. The saved rings themselves sit 0.164 r from the valley lines.

Why landing counts are low for every signal: 19 of the 82 saved rings are exactly the plane loop through their own anchor (1-3 anchors: the geodesic ring through the click on the saved ring's plane is the saved ring), i.e. not grooves at all, and the hover girdle at the same click is 25-87 degrees off the saved plane on most rings (preview radius 1.4-6x the saved one). Diagnostic rows in the table: the geodesic ring on the saved ring's own plane lands 23/82, the crease ring on the saved plane 7 landed / 20 near (mean 0.56 r, 0.130 r from valleys, 43 ms mean). So the plane a click implies, not the crease path, is the main miss; refitting the plane to the crease path (tried 1 and 3 rounds, inside traceGroove and inside the crease trace) did not help (6/11-12 landed/near at 240-360 ms; on the saved plane it got worse, 6/17) and was removed.

Timings on IMG_4109: SurfaceCreases.of 1.7-2.5 s once per model (PrincipalDirectionField + 9 Jacobi steps of 7 channels); a crease ring through given anchors and plane 43 ms mean (worst 312, mostly the spline fit; the double-cover Dijkstra is the minority); the one-click groove ring 117 ms mean, 407 worst; in the scene the V press on the carapace groove drafted in 34 ms after a 2458 ms first-use groove measurement. Full mvn test: 454 run, 0 failures (ring fingerprint tests unchanged; geodesic mode code is only re-indented under an if).

Verification: launch entry 'CRAW-60: groove rings (crawfish copy)' (ring-tool on ${workspaceFolder}/tmp/crawfish_rings.dsl). Screenshots tmp/craw60-hover-preview.png (hover preview beside ring_00) and tmp/craw60-groove-ring.png (V: the crease draft, pink with its 16 anchors, runs in the groove under the carapace edge where the saved ring_00, green, cuts straight across; 98% in a groove, 201 edges). Enter + Ctrl+S wrote creases = surface_creases(geometry=surface.geometry) and ring_85 = spline_ring(..., creases=creases.creases, ..., mode="crease") (kept as tmp/crawfish_rings.with-groove-ring.dsl; the launch copy was restored). Unit tests: CreaseRingTest (tilted-notch tube: groove ring in the notch < 0.04, geodesic > 0.2 off; crease statement reloads edge-exact; plain tube refused; ridge does not attract; V drafts / T switches / confirm / undo keep the mode), SplineRingChainTest.theSaveWiresOneCreaseFieldIntoEveryCreaseRing.
